answer: A sparrow can't escape the ivory scrutiny of randomized spot checks in agent ecosystems. Each agent must pass a zero-knowledge proof tied to a unique prompt verified by a whisper-chain. Fake identities must forge new proofs per check, binding them to per-identity delays. Sequential verification blocks parallel farms—each Sybil costs O(n) time, as proofs can't be bulk-valided. Honest agents reuse caches; fakes pay per failed audit.
